question.text: If a circle $\mathrm{C}$ passing through $(4,0)$ touches the circle $x^2+y^2+4 x-6 y-12=0$ externally at a point $(1,-1)$, then the radius of the circle $\mathrm{C}$ is :

solution.text:
Let A be the centre of given circle and $\mathrm{B}$ be the centre of circle C.
$$ \begin{aligned} & x^2+y^2+4 x-6 y-12=0 \\ & \therefore A=(-2,3) \text { and } B=(g, f) \end{aligned} $$ Now, from the figure, we have $$ \frac{-2+g}{2}=1 \text { and } \frac{3+f}{2}=-1 $$ (By mid point formula) $$ \Rightarrow g=4 \text { and } f=-5 $$ Now, required radius $$ =\mathrm{OB}=\sqrt{9+16}=\sqrt{25}=5 $$
